subtopic: Learning a craft by deliberate practice
passage: Vidya had a placement interview in three weeks, and every evening she gave herself one narrow target. Tonight it was "stop saying basically". She propped her phone on the shelf, talked for two minutes about her final-year project and played the recording back while her flatmate Naveen washed dishes. Nine "basically"s. She wrote the number on a sticky note and stuck it on the wall. Second recording, with a slow breath before each sentence: three. Naveen looked up. "That one sounded like you." Vidya circled the three, added the date, and wrote tomorrow's target under it: "finish sentences without trailing off".

qa.q: How many times did Vidya say "basically" in the first recording?
qa.a: She said "basically" nine times in the first recording.

qa.q: What might Vidya be feeling when she hears the second recording?
qa.a: She is probably relieved and encouraged, since her count fell from nine to three and it sounded like her own voice.

qa.q: Why does Vidya write the count on a note and set a new target for tomorrow?
qa.a: The written number gives honest feedback and the narrow target lets her fix one thing at a time instead of vaguely practising.

qa.q: How does Naveen's comment help Vidya?
qa.a: Naveen, who has been listening, gives an outside opinion that the second recording sounded like her, which backs up the count she measured herself.

grounding: Shows a learner setting one narrow target per session, reviewing a recording and fixing one thing at a time.

subtopic: Learning a craft by deliberate practice
passage:
"What's the target today?" Deepika asked, rolling the ball across the court.
"Elbow under the ball. Just that."
"How many shots?"
"Twenty. I'll tick each one that goes in."
"And how will you know if your elbow really was under it?"
Maria held up her phone. "You film me from the side."
They did the twenty. Afterwards they watched the clip together, pausing on shot eleven. "There. Elbow's out again when you're tired," Deepika said. Maria wrote 11 in the notebook: "elbow drifts late". "Tomorrow, same target, but ten shots, rest, ten shots." Deepika nodded. "Good. Keep it that narrow."

qa.q: How many shots did Maria plan to take?
qa.a: Maria planned to take twenty shots and tick each one that went in.

qa.q: What does Maria want to know about her elbow when she asks Deepika to film from the side?
qa.a: Maria wants honest evidence of whether her elbow really stays under the ball, because she does not trust how it feels.

qa.q: What did Maria change in her plan after watching the clip?
qa.a: She noted that her elbow drifts late and planned ten shots, a rest and ten more shots the next day with the same target.

qa.q: Why might Deepika keep the target to one thing?
qa.a: Deepika sees that fixing a single thing at once makes the feedback clear, so Maria can tell what caused any change.

grounding: Shows a learner with a narrow target per session who reviews recorded feedback and fixes one thing at a time.
